tws-samsung-galaxy-buds4-pro.tagline: King of soundstage, amazing vocal timbre, superb mic
tws-samsung-galaxy-buds4-pro.review: The vocal timbre is great. Very clean, wide and clear. Front-to-back depth and top-to-bottom staging are much better than the Buds 3 Pro. The planar timbre is much better than the 3's. Still the king of transparency mode. ANC is better than the 3's. Downside: replacement eartips are still hard to find. (Review on his YouTube.)

tws-huawei-freebuds-pro-5.tagline: Superb mic, ready for iOS/Android/Windows, no ecosystem lock-in
tws-huawei-freebuds-pro-5.review: Samsung doesn't dare open its multipoint to iOS or non-Samsung Android; here nothing is locked. The app is on iOS and Android, and there's even one for macOS. The sound goes roughly the same way as the Buds4 Pro, but with more mids around 500 Hz. Very mid-forward overall; just watch the YouTube review. It takes EQ fine. Technicalities are great too, but for natural timbre I'd say Samsung and Sony still win slightly: the planar timbre here is still a little less natural. Still far better than the FreeBuds Pro 4, which was metallic and sharp. (Review on his YouTube.)

tws-sennheiser-momentum-true-wireless-5.tagline: Replaceable battery, best mic among bean-shaped TWS
tws-sennheiser-momentum-true-wireless-5.review: You can replace the battery yourself. Not much improvement over the 4, just a nicer fit. ANC is up and the mic is waaay better, even better than Sony's; for a bean-shaped TWS this is probably the best right now. Same tonality, same soundstage. (Review on his YouTube and a short reel.)

tws-soundcore-liberty-5-pro-max.review: The best noise reduction in the industry; the AI noise reduction is great. The sound is still U-shaped: very bassy, very high highs. The treble can be tamed now, the bass not yet. Timbre and staging don't improve much on the Liberty 4. ANC is excellent: tidy, without that sucked-in feeling. For Soundcore this ANC is a huge step and can rival Sony's LinkBuds. Very comfy fit. (Review and a comparison on his YouTube.)

tws-huawe-freebuds-neo.review: (Reviewed on his YouTube and in an Instagram carousel.)

tws-tozo-aerosound-pro-nc9-pro.review: Mic and ANC are better than the Pudding. Technicalities aren't far from the Pudding either, in my view. I could make the Aerosound a bit warmer than the Pudding, which still leans airy even after EQ. Both are good; it comes down to battery and looks. Those are the two bean-shaped TWS options: Pudding or Tozo. (Review on his YouTube.)

tws-moondrop-pudding.review: Wins on the bean shape, if that's what you like. The Space Travel 2 is fair value at its price, but its case doesn't close; this one does. Boomy in the sub-bass and bright around 8–11 kHz, but there's an 8-band parametric EQ. The mic isn't bad, better than the 4i. Separation and soundstage are better than the 4i, 4 Pro and Aerosound 6; ANC too.

tws-huawei-freebuds-se-5-max.review: More or less the same as the SE 4 ANC, but battery, mic and ANC are a bit better. The sound is about the same: shouty in the upper mids, though the SE 5 Max has more sub-bass extension and is a bit boomier. Fine after EQ. The main thing is that it has multipoint now; the SE 4 ANC doesn't. Stereo imaging isn't as wide as the EarFun 4i, but it's OK. On the 4i you can tone down the boomy sub and the treble air; the Huawei still leans a bit U-shaped after EQ.

tws-huawei-freebuds-se-4-anc.review: Great driver, far from the overhyped Baseus BP1 Pro. Good ANC, decent. Custom EQ. The default tonality is a bit too bassy and airy (typical Huawei U-shape), but the driver and the sense of room are good. For 299k it's almost too good. Its tonality beats Tozo's in my view: tidier, grander. Soundstage and imaging aren't at the EarFun Air Pro 4i's level yet. Killer, a no-brainer. STOP FUCKING BUYING 100k TWS. SAVE UP FOR THIS. 200–300k is the new benchmark. (Full review on his YouTube.)

tws-baseus-bp1-ultra.review: Same story: the EQ makes it worse. The default tuning isn't as bassy as the BP1 Pro any more; the treble drops off a lot, it's warm. Not much of an improvement. (Comparison on his YouTube.)

tws-bose-ultra-open-earbuds-2nd-gen.review: Good driver. The deepest lows of the earring-style (ear-cuff) designs, not as bright as Huawei or Oppo. Unique colours. 3-band EQ. Beyond that I honestly don't know what else to say. Not bad, it's just 4 million rupiah, man. (Review on his YouTube.)

tws-oppo-enco-clip-2.review: The best-sounding ear-cuff, tuned by Dynaudio. Only preset EQs, no custom one, but the presets are already very good. I use Dynamic, tuned toward Dynaudio's house speaker sound: the deepest sub-bass of any ear-cuff open-ear. Pure Vocal is also good if you like vocal/mid-centric sound with less air and sub. (Review on his YouTube.)

tws-earfun-clip-2.review: A little bright, but the mic has improved and there's a custom EQ, so you can bring the treble down to be safe. Good price and physical buttons. (Review on his YouTube.)

iem-yu9-que-mercury.review: If you find the upper mids on the Reference or other CrinEar sets too high, try this. The air is fairly safe too, and the treble is smooth, nothing weird. The Melody has cleaner low mids than the regular Que.

iem-gk-kunten-pro.review: The tuning is muddier and dirtier than the regular Kunten, and the upper mids drop a little, so it's warmer and thicker. Just get the regular Kunten. The budget is awkward: you might as well go to ~300k for the Wenji, Tin Huo, Wyvern, Red Lion and so on.

iem-kefine-loric.review: Mild V, slightly muddy, and a bit shouty in the upper mids and lower treble. Not my preference. His "Gunsan Basshead" EQ is in the right-hand column of the sheet. (Review on his YouTube.)

headphone-wireless-sony-wh-1000xm6.review: The perfect lifestyle wireless headphone. World-class ANC. Superb vocal timbre. A 10-band EQ, flexible enough to set the tonality you want, on a base that's already balanced, with a bit more low mid around 100–200 Hz. The best vocal timbre I've heard on a wireless headphone; smooth, velvety highs. Bass isn't as heavy as the Momentum 4. ANC better than the QC Ultra. Microphone quality unmatched by other brands, really. The best wireless headphone so far, as a wireless one, not as a wired one. Main drawback: no wired mode over USB-C, though you can use it on Bluetooth while it charges. (Full review and a three-headphone comparison on his YouTube.)

headphone-wireless-sennheiser-hdb-630.review: The tuning is even more accurate and natural, with less sub-bass than the Momentum. A missed opportunity: it comes with a dongle, but not a 2.4 GHz gaming one, a Bluetooth transmitter for aptX Lossless instead. A shame, it's half-way. Clean mid-bass, superb punch, clarity and separation. The earpads are less roomy than JBL's or Bose's. And my rule still stands: NO PRICE ABOVE THE AIRPODS MAX. Brands like this have to price below the AirPods Max, or they'll have a hard time selling. (Review on his YouTube.)

headphone-wireless-sennheiser-momentum-4.review: Top-class, best-sounding high-end headphone for those who still want bass. Not neutral like the Stax S3. Quality is like a wired closed-back. The mic is nice and clear, not far from the XM5; the XM5 wins with lots of wind and café noise, but the Momentum 4 isn't far behind. FRAUNHOFER SOUND PERSONALISATION IS GREAT! (XM6 vs Momentum 4 vs QuietComfort Ultra comparison on his YouTube.)

headphone-wireless-earfun-wave-pro-x.tagline: Best sound in the mid budget
headphone-wireless-earfun-wave-pro-x.review: The best at 2 million rupiah for sound and fit. ANC competes with the Ult Wear and CH730; only the mic falls short. The default sound is bad: very sharp at 8–10 kHz and very boomy bass, untidy. But the driver really is detailed and clear, with great impact, punch and timbre after EQ. He submitted his EQ in Shenzhen on 23 Oct 2026; until it ships it's in the sheet.

headphone-wireless-earfun-tune-pro.review: Basically a Wave Pro + Space Pro. More bass than the Wave Pro, technically almost the same. Not too neutral, not as boomy as the Space Pro either. 2-year warranty, comes with a case, cheaper than the Space Pro. The best ANC too, in seal and comfort of the ANC algorithm. Downside: the fit isn't as roomy as the Wave Pro. (Review on his YouTube.)

headphone-fiio-jt1.review: Closed-back. Surely a very well-tuned neutral headphone, with great vocals. The bass isn't boomy or even boosted. Very comparable to the SHP9500 in tuning, with less bright upper mids.

headphone-snowsky-nature.review: Even cheaper than the JT1. A lot of low mid is cut around 200 Hz, but you can't go wrong at this budget. Your only other option is the ATH-M20x, which is on-ear and sounds much worse, or hunting for a Superlux without a detachable cable or with poor build. This one is well built, with a metal headband, and the over-ear fit is roomy and comfortable. His EQ is in the right-hand column of the sheet.
